In short

Office plants on rent means you pay a fixed monthly charge instead of buying plants outright. Online Plants Cart supplies the plants and planters, sends a trained gardener on a scheduled visit to water, clean and prune them, and swaps out any plant that fades, at no extra cost. Plans run across Gurgaon, Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad, and there is no purchase cost at the start.

Why offices rent plants instead of buying them

Almost every office that buys plants outright ends up in the same place about eight months later. Half the plants look tired, nobody is quite sure whose job the watering was, and someone in admin is getting quotes to replace them. Renting removes that cycle by making the plants somebody else's responsibility, permanently.

What the monthly figure covers

One charge covers the plants, the planters, delivery and placement, a scheduled visit by our gardener, and replacement of anything that stops looking well. There is no separate maintenance invoice and no per plant replacement charge.

How it looks on your books

Renting shifts the spend from a capital purchase to a monthly operating expense, which is often easier to approve than a one time number. It also removes the awkward asset that nobody wants to account for when the office is refitted.

When buying makes more sense

If you have a facility team who genuinely look after the plants, and you expect to stay in the same office for years, buying is cheaper over a long enough horizon. We will supply the plants at wholesale rates and sell you a maintenance contract separately. It is a perfectly reasonable way to do it and we will not push you off it.

Choosing plants for a real office, not a photograph

The constraint in most offices is light, not floor space. A large open floor with glass on one side has a bright edge and a dim middle, and the plants that thrive in the first three metres will slowly fail at fifteen. Matching the species to the position is most of the job.

Plants for cabins and workstations

Snake plant, ZZ plant, money plant and small aglaonema. Compact, tolerant of low light, and undemanding enough to survive a week when the occupant is travelling.

Plants for reception and lobbies

Areca palm, raphis palm, dracaena and large ficus in a good planter. Reception is where a plant does the most work for you, and it is worth spending more per plant and fewer of them.

Plants for meeting rooms and corridors

Peace lily, philodendron and syngonium. Peace lily earns its place in a meeting room by visibly drooping when it is thirsty, which makes it the one plant your team can read without training.

Air purifying plants

Snake plant, areca palm, money plant, peace lily and spider plant are the varieties most often asked for under this heading. They are excellent office plants for many reasons. The air purification effect in an occupied, ventilated office is real but modest, and we would rather say that plainly than sell it as a filtration system.

What we avoid recommending

Flowering plants for permanent indoor positions, anything needing direct sun in an interior cabin, and large specimens in narrow corridors where they will be knocked every day. All three look good in a proposal and disappoint within a season.

How many plants your office needs

A workable starting point is one medium plant for every three to four workstations, plus larger floor plants at reception, in each meeting room, and at the ends of long corridors. Then the plan gets adjusted for the thing that actually decides it, which is where the daylight falls.

Send us a floor plan or a short walkthrough video and you will get a plant count that reflects your office rather than a formula. On most sites the number comes out a little lower than the client expected, and the result looks better for it.

How the rental works

  1. Site visit or photographs

    We look at light, layout and how the space is used. For smaller offices, clear photographs and a floor area are enough to start.

  2. Plant plan and one monthly figure

    You get a proposed plant list by position, a planter selection, and a single monthly rental covering everything.

  3. Delivery and placement

    We deliver and place the plants outside your working hours where possible, so nobody is working around a trolley.

  4. Scheduled care visits

    Weekly or fortnightly, for watering, cleaning, pruning and pest checks, with a short written note left after each visit.

  5. Replacement without a conversation

    If a plant fades, it is swapped on the next visit. You do not need to report it, approve it or pay for it.

Where we provide office plant rental

We run plant rental across Gurugram, Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad, including the business districts where most of our clients sit: Cyber City and Golf Course Road in Gurugram, Sector 62 and the Noida Expressway corridor, Aerocity, Nehru Place and Connaught Place in Delhi.

Rental, or maintenance for plants you already own

Not every office needs a rental. If you already have plants and simply need someone competent to keep them alive, our plant maintenance contracts cover exactly that, including plants we did not supply.

For a striking feature in a reception area, a vertical garden often does more than any number of floor plants. For short term offices and events, look at event plant rental instead.

Frequently asked questions

What is included in the monthly office plant rental?

The plants, the planters, delivery, placement, and a scheduled visit by our gardener for watering, cleaning, pruning and pest checks. If a plant stops looking healthy, we replace it during that visit and you pay nothing extra.

There is no separate maintenance bill. One number covers the lot.

Is renting cheaper than buying office plants?

Over a two year horizon, buying is usually cheaper on paper. Renting wins when you count the things the paper leaves out: the plants that die because nobody was sure whose job it was to water them, the pots that no longer match after a refit, and the admin time spent arranging replacements.

Renting also moves the cost from capital expenditure to a monthly operating expense, which many finance teams prefer.

How many plants does an office actually need?

As a rough starting point, one medium plant for every three to four workstations, plus larger floor plants at reception, in meeting rooms and at the ends of long corridors.

But the useful answer comes from the floor plan. Light is the real constraint, not area. A deep floor plate with few windows will take fewer plants than its size suggests, and forcing more in just gives you plants that slowly decline.

Which plants work best in an air conditioned office?

Snake plant, ZZ plant, aglaonema, money plant, philodendron and areca palm handle continuous air conditioning and low natural light better than almost anything else. Peace lily works well too and has the advantage of visibly drooping when thirsty, which makes it a useful indicator plant.

We avoid recommending anything that needs direct sun or high humidity for a standard office cabin, however good it looks in the catalogue.

How often does your gardener visit?

Weekly or fortnightly, depending on the plan you choose and how the plants are doing. Newly installed plants settle better with weekly visits for the first month, after which many offices move to fortnightly.

Visits are scheduled outside your peak hours wherever possible, so nobody is working around a watering can during a client meeting.

What is the minimum contract period?

Six months is the usual minimum, and twelve months carries a better monthly rate. Shorter terms are possible for temporary offices and project sites, priced a little higher because the logistics cost the same whether the plants stay six weeks or six months.

Do you provide the pots, or do we?

We provide them as part of the rental, and you choose the finish from our range so the planters suit your interiors rather than fighting them.

If your architect has already specified planters, we are happy to work with those instead. In that case the rental drops slightly, and we take no responsibility for drainage problems caused by planters without proper holes.

What if a plant dies?

We replace it, free, as part of the contract. That is the point of renting rather than buying.

The one exception is damage from something outside normal office use, such as a plant knocked over during a move or used as an ashtray. Even then we usually just replace it and mention it once.

Can we rent plants for a short term project office?

Yes. Project offices, site offices and temporary floors are common requests, and we handle both the installation and the removal at the end.

For anything under a month, look at our event plant rental instead. It is built for short durations and priced for them.

Do office plants really improve air quality?

Modestly, and less dramatically than most marketing suggests. The often quoted NASA study was run in sealed chambers, and you would need a very large number of plants to match the effect of a decent ventilation system in a real office.

What the research does support more strongly is the effect on people. Employees in offices with plants report better concentration and lower stress, and that is usually the reason worth spending on.
